title: Roadstorm versioned tactical-intent fixture (schema version 1)
description: Fixture contract for the TacticalIntent record contract in tactical_intent.schema.json, defined at M0.9 from docs/OPPONENT_AI.md ('Architecture', 'Shared schema version 1', 'Implementation and acceptance') and docs/BENCHMARKS.md ('AI metrics'). A fixture fixes one scenario (participant, road/car geometry, difficulty, style, producer) and carries one or more intent records sampled at the 5 Hz tactical cadence, plus the behavioral expectations the fixtures/intent validator checks semantically (decode consistency, pace decode consistency, label thresholds, commitment hold, executed drift preference, sampling cadence, age arithmetic, difficulty age, context agreement, reset masking, safety deferral, intervention window, emergency consistency, correction materiality, intent identity, one-participant record sequence, source-observation linkage) and the documented initial acceptance metrics. Like handling_fixture.schema.json, this is a text contract: numeric values are authored initial values or documented targets, never measurements. A value that is not yet determined is JSON null and MUST be listed in 'unknowns'; the validator enforces that pairing for the null-meaning-undetermined fields. A referenced observation record that the observation slice does not ship MUST be listed in 'illustrative_sources', so a broken reference stays distinguishable from an intentional illustration. Companion vocabulary lives in ../common.schema.json. This fixture defines no model, weights, export or training interface; the learned-policy producer kind exists so the shared contract can be exercised, not because a trained model exists.

schema_version.description: Contract revision identifier. A fixture whose schema_version differs is rejected, not silently migrated. 1.1.0 matches tactical_intent.schema.json's 1.1.0 record revision (M0.9 independent schema checkpoint, 2026-11-27).

fixture_family.description: Which intent behavior the fixture exercises. 'regression' is reserved for fixtures added later for meaningful new concerns.

revision.description: Fixture content revision. Any semantic change to context, records, expectations or metrics bumps this and recomputes content_hash.

status.description: provisional = authored initial contract, not yet executed against an implementation; frozen = accepted after review; example = contract illustration that deliberately instantiates an unratified producer (learned_policy or cloning_only_policy) without claiming it exists. 'measured' is not valid here: fixtures carry targets and requirements, never measured outcomes.

tick_rate_hz.description: Fixed simulation tick rate (TECHNICAL_DESIGN 'Fixed tick and movement ownership').

road_width_m.description: Usable road width of the scenario section. GAME_DESIGN course widths generally range 9-20 m.

car_width_m.description: Car width, bounded by the initial TECHNICAL_DESIGN envelope 1.7-2.2 m.

producer_revision.description: Producer revision shared by every record in this fixture; records must agree with it.

traffic_age_is_difficulty_default.description: true when every record's traffic_age_ticks must equal the difficulty default (18/12/7). false lets a fixture exercise a non-default age, which then must be explained in the description.

records.description: Intent records in ascending sampled_tick order. With two or more records, consecutive generated_tick values must be 12 ticks apart (5 Hz at 60 Hz).

expectations.description: Behavioral expectations the validator checks. Each names a semantic check the validator implements and the record it applies to; a check id the validator does not implement is a fixture error, so expectations cannot drift from the executable checks.

metrics.description: Documented initial targets from OPPONENT_AI.md 'Implementation and acceptance'. A metric with status 'measured' is invalid in a fixture file; measured values belong to evaluation records. The bound members each comparator may carry follow schemas/common.schema.json's acceptance_metric allOf rules (threshold comparators carry value, range/ratio_range carry value_min/value_max, report carries no bound); fixtures/intent/validate_intent_contract.py enforces both rules semantically because its JSON Schema subset does not evaluate if/then.

unknowns.description: Every null in a record field whose null means 'not yet determined' (lateral.legal_corridor_half_width_m, lateral.decoded_offset_m, pace.speed_profile_interval_m_s, pace.target_speed_m_s, commitment.hold_window_s, interpolation.curve) must have a matching entry here, keyed by the dotted path including the record index, e.g. records.0.pace.target_speed_m_s. Entries may also record unratified decisions that have no null field.

illustrative_sources.description: Observation IDs a record references as illustration although the observation slice ships no such record. The validator's source_observation check resolves every source_observation_id against the shipped positive observation fixtures; an ID that resolves must agree on participant, decision timing (generated_tick may not precede the observation's sampled_tick and may lag it by at most one 5 Hz sampling period, the documented 0-200 ms planning phase), difficulty, style, traffic age, reset generation, history validity and route frame, and an ID that does not resolve must be declared here. The local section road width is not compared: observation features 14/19/24 describe the road 20/50/100 m ahead, which may legitimately differ from the scenario section's local width, and local width is checked by the decode/geometry rules. A declared illustrative ID may back only one record, exactly like a resolved one. Declaring an ID that does resolve is itself a failure, so the list stays an honest record of deliberate gaps (for example the follow-on observation of a second 5 Hz record) rather than a way to skip verification.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 over canonical JSON (sorted keys, compact separators, UTF-8) of this file with the content_hash member removed. Recomputed by the validator on every check.

check.description: Semantic check implemented by fixtures/intent/validate_intent_contract.py. The two metric checks apply to the fixture's comparison.metrics array (path 'comparison.metrics' or 'comparison.metrics.N'), not to a single record. Their ids match the metric checks of the scenario and handling slices so all three contracts check the shared acceptance_metric vocabulary identically.

path.description: What the expectation applies to: a record ('records.0'), the whole record sequence ('records', for cadence), or the fixture's metric array ('comparison.metrics', or one metric 'comparison.metrics.0').

statement.description: Human-readable restatement of the specified behavior being checked.
